newsitem.title: USA: ITT Hartford units' ratings cut by S&P.
newsitem.headline: ITT Hartford units' ratings cut by S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 24 - Standard & Poor's lowered its ratings of the ITT Hartford group of companies (Hartford) as shown in the list below. The ratings outlook for ITT Hartford Group Inc. is stable.

The rating action is based primarily on increased concern with the overall strength of Hartford's consolidated capital. Partially offsetting this is a superior business position within the markets that Hartford operates.

While Standard & Poor's expects capitalization to continue to improve from previous levels, it is now the company's view that such levels are no longer supportive of a double-A'-plus rating. This view incorporates the rapid growth in life revenue and assets, as well as risk-based capital measures and a destacked operating leverage tolerance (excluding affiliates) for Hartford Fire of 3 to 1, which Standard & Poor's does not consider as acceptable for the prior rating.

While capital needs should diminish, especially as the life subsidiary is able to self-finance its growth, Standard & Poor's believes capital adequacy ratios will only gradually return to more supportive levels.
Hartford Fire has enjoyed consistently strong operating results; however, returns on revenue have only slightly exceeded those of the industry over the last five years.
Results during the first half of 1996 were impacted adversely by unusually high catastrophe losses experienced during the first quarter of the year.

Operating performance of the life operations has been strong, with an average pretax return on assets of .70% over the past five years. Life earnings are supported by a low expense structure and well priced products.

Hartford maintains a superior business position with a well-defined commercial lines book and AARP-endorsed personal lines products. Furthermore, Standard & Poor's views Hartford Life as one of the leading annuity writers in the United States, with success in both fixed and variable markets.

While premium growth in the domestic property-casualty businesses has been flat, consistent with the industry, growth in life premiums and deposits have been strong, increasing from $6 billion in 1991 to $16 billion in 1995. This strong growth continued through the first six months of 1996, with Hartford leading the market in variable annuity sales.
This rating action assumes continued significant capital raising initiatives on the part of Hartford over the next year.

These initiatives, in combination with continued improvement in operating earnings, excluding any unusual charges, should allow the group to improve its overall capital position. The spin-off from ITT has enabled the group to access external capital and gradually grow funds internally, as dividend requirements have been greatly reduced, Standard & Poor's said.
Hartford Life Insurance group of companies (Hartford Life):
Hartford Life and Accident Ins. Co.
ITT Hartford Life and Annuity Ins. Co.
ITT Hartford Int'l Life Reassurance Corp.
ITT London and Edinburgh Ins. Co. Ltd.
